name: Stope charging and blasting (one firing)
summary: Production miners charge and fire each group of longhole rings in a stope, retreating from the slot raise along three 15 m sub-levels. Before charging they wait for the drawpoints to make room, measure and clear the holes, collect stick emulsion and detonators from the magazine and carry them up the Alimak raise. The supervisor approves the loaded stope, the blast is fired at end of shift, and the next shift examines it for misfires and frozen rings. Blocked holes, misfires and waiting for void are what slow it down.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-600 tonne-per-day underground longhole mine with ramp and shaft access, a 1,000-1,200 tonne-per-day mill and about 280 rotational site staff in northern Ontario.
baseline.notes: Site practice follows the Eagle River mine as described in its 2016 and 2022 technical reports, with Ontario Regulation 854 for the statutory checks. Crews work two 12-hour shifts a day on a 14-days-on, 14-days-off rotation.

unit_of_work: one stope firing (slot raise or ring group)
trigger: A drilled ring group is ready and the drawpoints have made enough void for it to be blasted.
end_state: The rings are fired, examined and the broken ore released to the mucking crews.

volume.seasonality: No seasonal pattern; firings follow the stope sequence, so the count rises when several stopes are in their blasting phase at once.

evidence.note: About 6 stopes a month in the organisation file; the 2022 report describes a slot raise plus longitudinal retreat on three 15 m sub-levels, which the author takes as 4-7 firings per stope.

surge.cause: several stopes reach the blasting phase together after a delay in drilling or backfill

evidence.note: Author's estimate from the bunching of stope cycles.

Production miners drill and blast longhole stopes; about 6 of the 16 production miners' FTE goes to checking, charging and firing (the rest is longhole drilling and cable bolting). The split is the author's estimate.
Assigning the charge crew, inspecting the loaded stope, guarding and firing, and the post-blast examination; about 1.5 hours per firing.
Making up the stick emulsion and detonator order for each firing and taking back returns; about 30 minutes per firing.
Checking the drill report against the ring design and reviewing blast results; about 45 minutes per firing.

systems.name: Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Mine design and scheduling software (3D design, scheduling)
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Magazine sign-out and blast log books (paper)

resources.name: Underground utility fleet (scissor lifts and light vehicles)

steps.name: Wait for void from the previous firing
steps.description: Before the next ring group can be charged, LHD operators must pull enough broken ore from the drawpoints to give the new blast room to swell. The supervisor checks the drawpoint tonnage against the engineer's void requirement and puts the charge-up on the line-up when it is met.

error.defect_description: Charge-up scheduled with too little void, risking a frozen or choked blast.

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.5: the LHD shrinks the broken ore, pulling only enough to create void for the next blast. Waiting time is the author's estimate for 4-8 firings per stope over a 3-6 week stope cycle.

steps.name: Check the drill report against the ring design
steps.description: The mine engineer compares the driller's report of hole lengths, dips and any lost holes with the ring design in the mine planning software, marks holes that need re-drilling and issues the charging sheet showing explosive per hole, primer positions and delay numbers.

error.defect_description: Charging sheet does not reflect a deviated or short hole.

control.basis: Site blasting standard: each firing is charged to an engineered ring design and charging sheet

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.5: 13-18 m down-holes of 64 mm on a 3-2-3 pattern with 0.9 m burden and 1.2 m spacing, retreating from the slot raise. Review time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Order explosives and detonators from the magazine
steps.description: The powder attendant makes up the stick emulsion cases, primers and non-electric detonators listed on the charging sheet, signs them out of the underground magazines against the crew's name and records the quantities in the magazine log.

error.defect_description: Wrong delay series or too few primers issued.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 127(1) (underground magazine under the control and direction of a competent person) and the federal magazine licence

evidence.note: 2022 s. 18.6.1: explosives and detonators arrive weekly and are moved into underground explosives and detonator magazines. Reg. 854 s. 127(1).

steps.name: Transport explosives and travel to the stope
steps.description: Two production miners load the explosives and detonators in separate boxes on the explosives vehicle, drive down the ramp to the stope's top access and, for captive sub-levels, carry them up the Alimak raise to the drilling sub-level. Touch time is the crew's elapsed travel time.

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.5: captive sub-levels are reached only through the Alimak raise. Travel time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Examine the sub-level and measure the holes
steps.description: The crew scales and checks the ground and screen on the sub-level, then blows out each hole with compressed air and measures its depth with a tape or loading hose. They compare the depths with the charging sheet and mark blocked, short or broken-through holes.

error.defect_description: A blocked hole is not found and is charged short.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 66(1) (ground conditions examined before work begins) and s. 67.1 (no other work during scaling)

evidence.note: Reg. 854 ss. 66(1), 67.1. The 2016 report notes woven screen in longhole sill backs to catch small loose during the loading cycle. Share of firings needing re-drill is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Re-drill or clean out blocked holes
steps.description: A production miner brings the small longhole drill back to the sub-level and re-drills or cleans out the blocked holes, or the engineer approves charging around them. Re-drilling can push the charge-up to the next shift.

error.defect_description: Re-drilled hole deviates and still does not reach the design toe.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; squeezing and broken ground near open stopes commonly block a share of holes.

steps.name: Prime and charge the holes with stick emulsion
steps.description: The miners make up primers with non-electric detonators, push them to the toe of each hole and load stick emulsion with the pneumatic loader to the collar height on the charging sheet, leaving the stemming length. They keep a running count of cases used per hole.

error.defect_description: Hole overcharged or undercharged against the design, causing overbreak or a frozen ring.

control.basis: Site explosives handling procedure and Ontario Regulation 854 s. 144 (no vehicle over loaded holes unless a supervisor-adopted procedure allows it)

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.5: all blast holes are loaded with stick emulsion using pneumatic loaders. Duration is the author's estimate for a 2-person crew charging 10-20 holes of 13-18 m.

steps.name: Tie in the delays and check against the sheet
steps.description: The crew connects the detonator leads to the trunk line in the delay sequence on the charging sheet, counts every connection and walks the round a second time to check for missed holes. The firing line is run back to the blasting station.

error.defect_description: A hole left off the trunk line, leading to a misfire.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 141.1(1): only the worker who makes the final connections may fire the blast

steps.name: Return unused explosives to the magazine
steps.description: Left-over stick emulsion and detonators are carried back and returned to the magazines, and the powder attendant records the returns so that the issued amount minus the return equals the explosive used in this firing.

error.defect_description: Returns not recorded, so magazine stock and powder factor are wrong.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 128(5): explosives not attended must be returned to storage, not left at the workplace

steps.name: Inspect the loaded stope and approve the blast
steps.description: The shift supervisor walks the loaded sub-level, checks the tie-in and the charging sheet, confirms that drawpoints below are empty of people and equipment and that the brow barricades are up, and puts the stope on the end-of-shift blast list.

error.defect_description: An approach left unguarded on the blast list.

control.basis: Site blasting procedure: supervisor inspection before a stope blast is placed on the blast list

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Wait for blasting time and clear the area
steps.description: Stope blasts are fired at the end of shift when the mine is cleared. Before firing, a worker is posted at every entrance to the blast area, the blaster shouts or sounds the warning and confirms that everyone has left.

error.defect_description: A person not accounted for in the cleared area.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 141(1)(a) and (b): guard posted at each entrance, warning given and confirmation that all persons have left

evidence.note: Reg. 854 s. 141(1). End-of-shift blasting is common Ontario practice; the wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Fire the blast and lock out the firing circuit
steps.description: The blaster who made the final connections initiates the blast from the firing station, then disconnects and short-circuits the firing line and locks the blasting switch open. The blast time is written in the blast log.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 141.1(1) (firing by the worker who made the final connections) and s. 149(c) (firing cables removed, short-circuited and the switch locked open before anyone returns)

steps.name: Wait for fumes to clear and seismic activity to settle
steps.description: No one returns until ventilation has cleared the blast fumes and, in seismically active areas, until the post-blast hold has passed. The blast area stays barricaded through shift change.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 147 (minimum waiting periods before return) and the site post-blast re-entry procedure

evidence.note: Reg. 854 s. 147 sets minimum waiting periods; Macassa issues post-blast seismicity reports every 12 hours. Duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Examine the blasted stope from the drawpoints
steps.description: The next shift's supervisor examines the drawpoints and the sub-level from outside the brow, looking for misfired holes, cut-offs, hang-ups and damage to ground support, and tests for gas before mucking is allowed.

error.defect_description: Cut-off hole not seen and found later during mucking.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 63(1): supervisor examines places where drilling and blasting occur during each shift

evidence.note: Reg. 854 s. 63(1). Outcome shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Report and record the misfire
steps.description: The supervisor reports the misfire to the mine captain, barricades the area and writes it in the shift log. The misfired charge is not pulled out; it is re-primed and fired at the next safe blasting time.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 137(1), (3) and (4): misfired charge not withdrawn, blasted without undue delay, reported and recorded in the shift log

steps.name: Re-prime and re-blast the misfired holes
steps.description: A production miner washes out or exposes the misfired hole collars, places new primers as the blasting procedure allows, ties in and the area is fired again at the next blasting time.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 137(1): misfire blasted without undue delay at a time when no worker is exposed

evidence.note: Reg. 854 s. 137(1). Duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess a frozen or hung-up ring with the engineer
steps.description: When part of a ring did not break or the broken ore has bridged, the supervisor and the mine engineer look at the drawpoint and the sub-level, decide whether to re-drill, re-charge with extra relief or wait for more void, and record the decision.

error.defect_description: Remedy chosen that leaves ore behind in the stope.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; frozen rings and bridged muck are the common longhole blasting problems.

steps.name: Record the blast in the blast and shift logs
steps.description: The supervisor records the stope, rings fired, explosive used, delays and any problems in the blast log and shift report, and enters the estimated broken tonnes in the production spreadsheet.

error.defect_description: Explosive quantity or rings fired recorded wrongly.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Review blast results and update the next ring design
steps.description: The mine engineer reviews the post-blast report, powder factor and drawpoint observations, and changes the charging for the next ring group where the last one broke badly or showed overbreak. The review is usually done the same day and does not hold up mucking.

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.8: CMS surveys show an average of 1.0 m wall overbreak, which engineering accounts for in design. Review time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Release the broken ore for mucking
steps.description: The supervisor marks the drawpoints open on the line-up board, removes the blast barricades and tells the mucking crew how much ore to pull: only enough for the next void while blasting continues, or all of it after the last firing.

error.defect_description: Overpull instruction given while the stope still needs confinement.

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.5 describes partial pulls between blasts and fast mucking-out after the last blast.

exceptions.name: Blocked or short holes
exceptions.description: Holes are blocked by squeezing or broken ground and must be re-drilled before charging.

exceptions.name: Misfire
exceptions.description: One or more holes did not fire; the charge is re-primed and fired at the next blasting time and recorded in the shift log.

exceptions.name: Frozen or hung-up ring
exceptions.description: Part of the ring did not break or the muck bridged; the engineer decides whether to re-drill, re-charge or accept.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the drilled ring group being ready to its broken ore being released for mucking
benchmarks.population: Longhole stope firings at a narrow-vein Ontario gold mine

evidence.note: Author's estimate: one to three days waiting for void, one shift to charge, blasting at end of shift and re-entry the next shift; re-drills and frozen rings push some firings past a week.

benchmarks.unit: metres per production down-hole, 64 mm diameter

evidence.note: Section 16.5.

benchmarks.unit: metres average between hangingwall and footwall measured by CMS

evidence.note: Section 16.8.

pain_points.description: Charging waits for the drawpoints to make enough void, so blasting and mucking of the same stope hold each other up.

evidence.note: Partial pulls between blasts are the site's dilution control (s. 16.5); the waiting is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Captive sub-levels are reached only through Alimak raises, so carrying explosives in and out takes time and exposes the crew.

evidence.note: Sections 1 and 25 note lower productivity and higher injury potential from Alimak access to captive sub-levels.

pain_points.description: Blocked holes, frozen rings and misfires send work back to drilling or a second blast and cost a shift or more.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Stick emulsion loaded by hand with pneumatic loaders is slower than bulk emulsion, and the technical report recommends a change.

evidence.note: Sections 1 and 25 list bulk emulsion instead of stick powder as an improvement.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (SRK project CAPR001445, effective 31 December 2021)

assumptions: A case is one firing (a slot raise or a group of rings), not a whole stope; a stope takes about 4-7 firings.
Crew steps (s04, s05, s07, s08, s11, s16) use people = 2 for the two-person charge crew, so labour hours are twice the touch time.
Firing is non-electric and done at end of shift from a firing station near the stope; central blasting from surface is not described in the sources for 2019-2022 and is not assumed.

The organisation's process map lists only prod-miner and ug-shift-supervisor; the workflow adds explosives-handler (magazine sign-out and returns) and mine-engineer (charging sheet and blast review), both from the organisation file.
Misfire, frozen-ring and re-drill shares are the author's estimates; no published rates for this mine were found.
